body.text: namo ratnatrayāya / nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya mahākāruṇikāya / namaḥ sarvasattvavyasanaghātine / namaḥ sarvasattvabhayapraśamanakarāya / namaḥ sarvasattvabhayottāraṇakarāya / namaḥ sarvavidyādhigatāya / namaḥ sarvavidyāvidhigatamūrtaye mahākāruṇikāya / namo mahāvidyārājaprāptaye mahāyogine /
body.translated_text: Homage to the <s>Triratna</s> (Three Jewels)! Homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s> (great being), the greatly compassionate one! Homage to the destroyer of all beings' calamities! Homage to the one who pacifies the fears of all beings! Homage to the one who rescues all beings from fear! Homage to the one who has mastered all <s>vidyās</s> (spells)! Homage to the greatly compassionate one whose form embodies all mastered <s>vidyās</s>! Homage to the one who has attained the great king of <s>vidyās</s>, the great <s>yogin</s>!

body.text: tasmai namaskṛtvā idamāryāvalokiteśvaramukhodgīrṇaṃ vajradharamahīyaṃ hayagrīvaṃ nāma paramahṛdayamāvartayiṣyāmisarvakarmārthasādhakam / asahyaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ yakṣāṇāṃ cavināśakam / amoghaṃ sarvakarmaṇāṃ viṣāṇāṃ ca nāśakam / tadyathā
body.translated_text: Having paid homage to him, I shall now recite this supreme <s>hṛdaya</s> (heart-spell) called <s>Hayagrīva</s> (Horse-Necked One), uttered from the mouth of the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, mighty as <s>Vajradhara</s>, the accomplisher of all aims and tasks, unbearable to all <s>bhūtas</s> (spirits), the destroyer of <s>Yakṣas</s>, unfailing in all actions, and the destroyer of poisons. It is as follows:

body.text: om tarula tarula vitarula vitarula sarvaviṣaghātaka jvalitavisphuliṅgāṭṭahāsa kesarāṭopapravṛddhavega vajrakhuranirghātaka calitavasudhātala niḥsvasitahasitamārutotkṣiptadharaṇīdhara parabhṛtagaṇasamūhavikṣobhaṇakara paravidyāsaṃbhakṣaṇakara sarvagrāhotsādanakara paramaśāntikarasarvagrahapraśamanakara budhya budhya dhāva dhāva ca bhagavā hayagrīva khāda khāda paramaṃtrām / rakṣa rakṣa kṣamasva kṣamasva sa mayābhihitāṃ mantrām / siddhiṃ me diśadiśa āviśa āviśa / ghorapiśāca sarvagraheṣvapratihato mama varavajradaṃṣṭra kiṃ cirāpayasi / idaṃ duṣṭagrahaṃ duṣṭasattvaṃ duṣṭapiśācaṃ vā dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna kampa kampa matha matha pramatha pramatha / tathāgatājñāṃ pālaya buddhadharmasaṃghānujñātaṃ me karma śīghraṃ
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ tarula tarula vitarula vitarula</s>! O destroyer of all poisons! O one with blazing, sparking, thunderous laughter! O one whose mane swells with surging force! O crusher with <s>vajra</s>-hooves! O shaker of the surface of the earth! O one whose exhalations and laughter are winds that lift up the mountains! O one who agitates the host of hostile <s>bhṛta</s>-beings! O devourer of hostile <s>vidyās</s> (spells)! O eradicator of all <s>graha</s> (malign seizures)! O supreme peacemaker and pacifier of all <s>grahas</s>! Awaken, awaken! Rush, rush, O blessed <s>Hayagrīva</s>! Devour, devour the enemy <s>mantras</s>! Protect, protect! Be patient, be patient with the <s>mantra</s> spoken by me! Grant me <s>siddhi</s> (accomplishment), grant! Enter, enter! O terrible <s>piśāca</s> (flesh-eating spirit), among all <s>grahas</s> you are unobstructed! O one with supreme <s>vajra</s>-fangs, why do you delay? This wicked <s>graha</s>, this wicked being, this wicked <s>piśāca</s> — shake, shake! Violently shake, violently shake! Tremble, tremble! Crush, crush! Thoroughly crush, thoroughly crush! Uphold the command of the <s>Tathāgata</s>! The task sanctioned by the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s> — quickly

body.text: kuru kuru mā vilamba / hayagrīvāya phaṭ vajrakhurāya phaṭ vajradaṃṣṭrāya phaṭ vajradaṃṣṭrotkaṭabhayabhairavāya phaṭ / paravidyāsaṃbhakṣaṇāya phaṭ / paramantravināśakāya phaṭ / sarvagrahotsādakāya phaṭ / sarvaviṣaghātakāya phaṭ / sarvagraheṣvapratihatāya phaṭ / vaḍavāmukhāya phaṭ / sarvagrahapiśācān me vaśamānaya / yāvanto mamaye kecitahitaiṣiṇastān sarvān vaḍavāmukhena nikṛntaya phaṭ / namo nama āryāvalokiteśvarāya bodhisattvāya mahāsattvāya / sidhyantu mama maṃtrapadā hayagrīvo bhagavān ājñāpayati svāhā /
body.translated_text: do, do! Do not delay! To <s>Hayagrīva</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the <s>vajra</s>-hooved one, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the <s>vajra</s>-fanged one, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the terrifyingly fierce one with protruding <s>vajra</s>-fangs, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the devourer of hostile <s>vidyās</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the destroyer of enemy <s>mantras</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the eradicator of all <s>grahas</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the destroyer of all poisons, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the one unobstructed among all <s>grahas</s>, <s>phaṭ</s>! To the mare-faced one, <s>phaṭ</s>! Bring all <s>graha</s>-<s>piśācas</s> (seizing spirits) under my control! As many as there are who wish me harm — cut them all down with the mare's mouth, <s>phaṭ</s>! Homage, homage to the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the <s>Mahāsattva</s>! May my <s>mantra</s>-words be accomplished! The blessed <s>Hayagrīva</s> commands! <s>Svāhā</s>!

body.text: ayaṃ hayagrīvavidyā rājā paṭhitasiddhaḥ upacāraḥ ātmarakṣājāpena pararakṣā paṃcaraṃgīsūtram ekaviṃśatigranthayaḥ kṛtvā bandhitavyam / yāvajīvaṃ rakṣā kṛtā bhavati / ḍāinīgrahagṛhītasya pratikṛtiṃ kṛtvā piṇḍaśastreṇa chettavyā / sarvaparakṛtā maṃtrāśchinnā bhavanti sarvaśatravastambhanaṃ manasā vyavahāre svakham mukhe kṛtvā vidyā japtayā uttarāyati / spṛṣṭāveśaneṣusnātaṃ śucivastraprāvṛtaṃ śucau pradeśe sumanasāsaṃbaddhā āveśaye śuklavaliryathālaṃbhena / candragrahe sūryagrahe ghṛtaṃ tāmrabhājane kṛtvā tāvajjepadyāvaccandro mukto bhavati taṃ ghṛtaṃ pive medhāvī bhavati ekenoddeśena ślokaśatamudgṛṇhāti / padmāṃ juhe ghṛtamakṣayaṃ bhavati / atha sādhitumicchet / candanamayaṃ lokeśvarapratimā kartavyā / dakṣiṇenāryavajradharaḥ / vāmenāryāvalokiteśvaraḥ
body.translated_text: This <s>Hayagrīvavidyā</s> (Spell of Hayagrīva) is the king (of spells), perfected through recitation. The ritual procedure is as follows: through the <s>jāpa</s> (recitation) for self-protection, (one achieves) protection of others. A <s>pañcaraṅgīsūtra</s> (five-colored thread) should be tied with twenty-one knots; protection is established for as long as one lives. For one seized by a <s>ḍākinī-graha</s> (witch-seizure), an effigy should be made and cut with a sharp instrument. All enemy <s>mantras</s> are severed. For the paralysis of all enemies, having mentally (uttered the spell) in one's dealings and placed one's own hand on the mouth, one should recite the <s>vidyā</s> (spell), and it will rise up (in power). For those afflicted by touch or possession, (the person) having bathed, clad in clean garments, in a clean place, bound with flowers, should be subjected to possession (exorcism) with white offerings as appropriate. During a lunar or solar eclipse, having placed clarified butter in a copper vessel, one should recite (the spell) as long as the moon remains eclipsed; one who drinks that clarified butter becomes intelligent and can memorize a hundred verses at a single hearing. If one makes an offering with <s>padma</s> (lotus), the clarified butter becomes inexhaustible. Now, if one wishes to accomplish (the practice): an image of <s>Lokeśvara</s> (Lord of the World) should be made of sandalwood. On the right, the noble <s>Vajradhara</s>; on the left, the noble <s>Avalokiteśvara</s>

body.text: trimūrtiḥ kāryaḥ / sarvopari vaḍavāmukhaḥ paravidyāsaṃbhakṣaṇaḥ / tasyāgrataḥ ayaṃ hayagrīvavidyārājam aṣṭasahasraṃ japet / tataḥ sarvakarmāṇi kuryāt / spṛṣṭāveśanaṃ gugguladhūpena / satatajāpena sarvakāryasiddhirbhavati / sarvaḍāinī dṛṣṭamātrā vaśībhavati / bhasmanā sarṣapeṇa udakena sapta japtena rakṣā kartavyā / sīmābandhaḥ kṛto bhavati / sarvamudrāmokṣaṇam udakena vaśīkaraṇaṃ phalapuṣpādyaiḥ / ayaṃ paṭhitasiddhaḥ / asādhita eva sarvakarmāṇi kurute // 0 //
body.translated_text: [One should construct] a <s>trimūrti</s> (triple form of the deity); above all [others stands] <s>Vaḍavāmukha</s> (the mare-faced one), who consumes the highest knowledge (<s>paravidyā</s>; before him, one should recite this <s>Hayagrīvavidyārāja</s> (the sovereign <s>vidyā</s> of <s>Hayagrīva</s>) eight thousand times; thereafter one should perform all ritual acts; [one should perform] <s>spṛṣṭāveśana</s> (anointing the touched image) with incense of <s>guggula</s> (bdellium resin); by constant <s>jāpa</s> (repetition), success in all undertakings comes about; every <s>ḍākinī</s> (female spirit) is brought under control by mere sight; with ashes, mustard seeds, and water consecrated seven times by recitation, a protective rite should be performed; a <s>sīmābandha</s> (boundary seal) is thereby established; liberation of all <s>mudrās</s> (seals/gestures) [is achieved] through water, [and] subjugation through fruits, flowers, and other [offerings]; this [<s>vidyā</s>] is perfected by [mere] recitation; even without prior ritual preparation it accomplishes all ritual acts.
